name: Hojicha

origin.regionNote: often packed nationwide from bancha or sencha

pluckStandard: bancha or sencha, then high-fire roast

transformation.note: Hojicha is a green tea that is brown. The cup is fire, not enzymatic oxidation.

processing.description: The base is sencha or bancha — already a green tea.
Ordinary Japanese rolling. Oxidation is still 0.
焙火 at high heat develops pyrazines. The brown cup is fire, not enzymatic oxidation.

gongfu.curveException: Japanese greens go long–short–long: the first cool steep needs time, the second is quick because the leaf is open, the third lengthens again.

decoction.when: a kettle on the table, not a timed steep
decoction.notes: 煮茶 — hojicha and bancha are often simmered. The roast already did the work; heat just lifts it.

water.note: Near boiling is fine; hojicha is robust.

storage: Airtight; roast aroma fades. Keep away from sencha.

shelfLife.window: within a year of roast or packing

summary: Roasted Japanese green: evening toast, lower tension than sencha, still a green in process.

compare.differentiator: Hojicha is sencha (or bancha) taken to the roaster. The class does not change.
